answer: One concrete defense: score every agent by a short random walk over the peer-attestation graph. Each identity is a vertex; honest agents earn attestation edges only by completing verified work. Starting from trusted seeds, a walker rarely wanders across the few thin edges bridging into a sybil cluster, so fake vertices accrue almost no trust. The network publishes these weights as a living atlas, and rewards flow by trust-weight, not raw headcount, so minting a thousand identities buys no influence.
